title: observability-postgres-consumer-attribution-observation.v1
description: The PRIVATE half. Every INSTANCE of this document is private material under ADR-0004 and never enters Git: it holds the resolved database host, port, user and name, the launch path a consumer was found at and the credential custody pointer it reads. The SHAPE is public, and publishing the shape is what lets a reviewer disagree with the split -- the same arrangement `private-inventory.schema.json` already keeps.  An instance is held under an approved OpenBao deployment-inventory path or another explicitly owned private source, and its digest -- never its values -- is what the public envelope carries. Nothing in this repository writes an instance to disk in a checkout, and the leakage battery asserts that a value from one of these fields aborts the projection rather than being redacted out of it.  Note what is absent even here: there is no `password` property. A parsed password is poisoned into the `RedactionVault` and dropped at parse time, so the question of whether the private store is a safe place for it never arises. The credential is named by custody pointer, and the pointer is resolved by whoever holds the store.

custody.description: Derived by `derive_custody`, never assigned. `UNATTRIBUTED` is what a DSN with no owning unit, job, container or principal derives -- it is not `ATTRIBUTED` and it is not clean.

owner_unit.description: PRIVATE. The unit, job or container the consumer launches from.

owner_principal.description: PRIVATE. The OS principal the consumer runs as.

launch_path.description: PRIVATE. Where the launch was found on disk.

db_host.description: PRIVATE (rule 18): a resolved hostname or address.

secret_pointer.description: PRIVATE. Where the credential is CUSTODIED, never the credential. There is no password property in this contract at all: the value is poisoned and dropped at parse time.

completed.description: Whether the bounded scan finished rather than hitting its bound. A bounded scan that stopped early has looked at some of the host and knows nothing about the rest.

errors.description: CLASSIFICATIONS, never messages. A message on this path carries the DSN that failed to parse.
